va_shenandoah_nw_va_region.blurb: This northwest Virginia region is anchored by Shenandoah National Park, where the climbing is strung out along the ridge-top drive that runs the length of the park. Bouldering makes up the biggest share, with traditional routes close behind and smaller amounts of sport and top-roping, plus a few ice lines. Old Rag is the largest single draw: massive granite, mostly trad lines and boulders. Elsewhere in the park there are boulder fields and top-rope walls. Roped climbs run mostly from 5.8 to 5.11 with a handful at 5.12, while boulder problems cluster between V0 and V6 and reach a good deal higher. Outside the park, Hidden Rocks, Elizabeth Furnace and Crescent Boulders add more crags and blocks.

ar_northwest_arkansas_nwa_region.blurb: Northwest Arkansas climbing is all on sandstone, in the countryside around Fayetteville and Bentonville. The rock is iron-rich and rough, with sturdy holds such as flakes, plates and chicken heads. Bouldering and sport climbing share most of the climbs, with a modest amount of trad. Sport routes sit mostly between 5.9 and 5.12, peaking at 5.10 with some harder lines above, and boulder problems cover everything from V0 to V6 and beyond. Lake Lincoln is the largest area, with both roped routes and plenty of boulders, and Fern, Fitzgerald Mountain and Bigfoot Hollow add more. Fitzgerald faces west, which keeps it pleasant when summer heat arrives.

wa_spokane_area.blurb: Spokane has a surprising amount of climbing close to town, with most crags a short drive from the city and many approaches of only a few minutes. Sport routes dominate, followed by bouldering and trad, with a little top-roping. Grades run mostly from 5.9 to 5.12 and peak at 5.10, with a solid band of 5.11 and 5.12 and a few harder lines. Granite is the main rock at Minnehaha, Dishman and McLellan Rocks, while Deep Creek, Cliff Drive and Liberty Park are on basalt. Minnehaha is the long-established favourite, with vertical to slabby faces; Dishman is steeper and harder; Tum Tum and McLellan hold much of the bouldering. Rocks of Sharon adds views across the Palouse.

wa_sw_tacoma.blurb: This large grouping stretches from Tacoma in the northwest to the Hood River end of the Columbia Gorge in the southeast, taking in the Mount Rainier country. The Columbia Gorge holds most of the climbing, on basalt: traditional routes on the big monolith of Beacon Rock, sport walls, and bouldering. Rock quality varies, but the river setting is scenic, and most approaches start from Portland. The Southwest Cascades mix sport, trad and top-rope with alpine routes around Rainier and some waterfall ice, while the Tacoma and I-5 foothills side is mostly sport and bouldering. Rope grades are mostly 5.9 to 5.11, with 5.10 the most common, and boulder problems stay mostly in the V0 to V5 range.

ca_big_bear_north.blurb: North of Big Bear Lake in the San Bernardino Mountains, this area is centred on Holcomb Valley Pinnacles, a granite zone sitting roughly 7,400 to 7,600 feet up among pines. The granite is heavily featured and mostly good quality, so steep-looking lines often go at moderate grades. Sport routes are the main draw, with trad lines that need only a standard rack, and bouldering is spread through Holcomb Valley and along the North Shore. Most roped climbs fall between 5.8 and 5.11, with 5.10 the most common, and most boulder problems are V0 to V4. Hanna Rocks is a quieter ridge of similar granite with room to explore. Climbing continues year-round depending on winter, and shade is prized in summer.

nm_jemez_mountains_and_jemez_valley.blurb: The Jemez Mountains, west of Los Alamos, offer varied volcanic and granite climbing at high altitude in river gorges and meadows. The rock changes from place to place: granite at Gilman Tunnels, rhyolite with excellent friction at Las Conchas, and welded tuff elsewhere. Sport routes are the most numerous, followed by trad and a large bouldering contingent, with Ponderosa Bouldering made up almost entirely of boulder problems. Roped grades run mostly from 5.10 to 5.12 and peak at 5.11, with some harder lines. The biggest groups are Capulin Canyon and Cochiti Mesa, Las Conchas and Upper East Fork. An autumn visit found warm, sunny days despite the elevation, and the setting is scenic and quiet.
